We've introduced native, agentic spreadsheet extraction 📊 into LlamaParse. 

Spreadsheets are a wildly different format from PDFs (or any other document format). They can span arbitrarily many rows/columns, lack any guarantees on tabular structure, and can have information linked across multiple sheets. The native ways to deal with spreadsheets is usually through a code interpeter as opposed to OCR.

We've introduced a tuned agentic engine (model+harness) that is equipped for large-scale schema guided extraction from spreadsheets. You can extract out dense sheets like balance sheets into clean structured fields. 

Check out the docs for how to integrate into the API: https://t.co/QPDs4RqxfW

On the UI, select "agentic plus", and see "spreadsheet options" in the advanced options section. 

Signup for LlamaParse here! https://t.co/flYnwVfvWZ

reviewedPosts.text:
如果 AI 要处理的是一个连标准答案都可能不存在的问题，只看最后答没答对，评测就不太够了。

最近看 Apodex 推出的 TRACES，我最关注的一点，是它开始认真评估 HOW AI DISCOVERS。

很多 benchmark 面对的还是已经定义好、答案已经存在的问题。但很多真实的科学发现是没有 answer key 的，甚至一开始连假设是否正确都不知道。中间需要找证据、调用工具、运行实验，根据反馈不断调整方向。

TRACES 沿着这个思路，把静态题库变成了可执行环境。

目前它构建了 17 个 environment、218 个 episode，里面会提供数据、文献、代码执行、专业工具、模拟器和实验反馈。被评估的也不只是底层模型，而是模型、harness、工具、记忆和控制策略组成的完整 solver。

更关键的是，TRACES 会同时验证结果和过程。

最终结果由 hidden outcome verifier 检查，完整 trajectory 则通过 process verification，被拆成 Tools、Repair、Alternatives、Coherence、Evidence、Scope 六个维度。

也就是看工具有没有用对，错误能不能及时修正，是否保留并更新竞争假设，长任务里状态和逻辑有没有跑偏，证据能否支撑结论，以及结论有没有超出证据本身的边界。

所以它给出的不只是一个总分，更像是一份 solver 的能力诊断。失败以后，可以进一步看到问题究竟出在工具、修错、假设管理、证据链还是长程一致性。

过程评分本身也有明确 rubric，并锚定到 trajectory 的具体步骤，再经过独立 review；出现分歧时会重新评分和 adjudication。

我觉得这对现在的 Agent 很重要。

任务走向长程和开放环境后，真正拉开系统差距的，往往就是中间持续发生的那些判断和修正。Apodex 把这个方向称为 Discoverative AI，而 TRACES 想先解决的，就是怎么把「AI 如何完成一次发现」变成可以验证、诊断和比较的东西。

Website： https://t.co/qqhV7seCVb

Hugging Face paper：https://t.co/h7GbBHXJeb

reviewedPosts.author: Xudong07452910
reviewedPosts.text:
Agent 一旦跑到几十步，最先失控的往往是记忆。

任务越长，上下文里会混进已经完成的步骤、过期信息和大量执行噪声。Agent 明明积累了很多经验，却越来越难判断「现在到底该调用哪条」。

Princeton、Stanford、Oxford、NUS 团队这篇论文提出 Recuris，把 Agent Memory 分成两部分：

Working Memory 持续记录当前进度、未完成目标和验证证据；Experiential Memory 保存过去积累的 Skills。

Agent 每走一步，都会根据「当前状态」选择需要的经验，再用环境反馈更新状态，而不是反复从整段历史里找答案。

更有意思的是，失败也会反过来更新记忆。

系统会从执行轨迹里定位问题出在哪个记忆组件，只修改对应部分，并通过独立验证后才保留这次更新。基础模型本身始终不变。

效果很明显：在 τ²-Bench 上，GPT-5.6 Sol 提升 17.8 个百分点，Claude Opus 5 提升 15.6 个百分点，达到 87.9%。任务越长，优势还会继续扩大，最长任务提升达到 32.2 个百分点。

长期 Agent 的记忆，可能更像一个会不断整理自己的工作区。

旧经验要能调用，当前状态要能更新，失败之后还要知道该改掉哪一部分。

这比单纯把更多内容塞进 Memory 里重要得多。

📎 arxiv: https://t.co/jOiBrzqGfV

reviewedPosts.author: fchollet
reviewedPosts.text:
To note, this isn't intelligence. This is skill. Superhuman skill. Of course it will *feel* like intelligence to anyone who equates intelligence with skill, which is probably almost everyone.

Intelligence in my definition is (and has always been) the efficiency with which you extract and operationalize the patterns you need to achieve a given level of skill. It's basically the ratio between your resources and what you can do with them, an information conversion ratio. It is not tied to any capability threshold. You can always achieve arbitrarily high skill with arbitrarily low intelligence, given arbitrarily high resources.

Humans will be left behind capability-wise in all verifiable domains, but remain many orders of magnitude more intelligent than current AI -- you didn't need 1,000,000x the code volume of all of GitHub in order to learn to code.

reviewedPosts.author: fchollet
reviewedPosts.text: One way to think of current AI is as a big sponge for patterns. It absorbs and operationalizes any pattern it is exposed to (albeit with very low data efficiency at training time). Once you can programmatically enumerate the complete space of patterns in a domain, saturating the domain becomes purely a matter of computational resources.
